author: aaronfranke
body:
The existing local player height code was a bit of a mess. This PR is my attempt at refactoring of it, though a few issues remain.

Benefits:
- Unified `BasisLocalHeightInformation` and `BasisHeightDriver` into `BasisLocalHeight`.
- The properties of `BasisLocalHeight` are read-only for public users, so setting these values is now encapsulated.
- Much clearer naming and separation of avatar vs player scale terms. Replace "default" with "fallback" for clarity.
- Introduce "RealUser" named properties as a way to properly refer to the real user's sizes.
  - These currently aren't read from elsewhere in the codebase, which is a problem.
- Avatar heights/scales are now saved and loaded per-avatar, allowing different avatars to have different scales.
- New ability in the code to set the height as a scale multiplier instead of an amount of meters via `BasisHeightMeasurement.ScaleMultiplier`. Could be exposed in the UI later.
- New functions in `BasisDataStore` to save and load JSON in a well-formatted cross-platform way.
- The near clipping plane will automatically pull itself closer inwards when using a small avatar, which tries to avoid the avatar becoming invisible or the menu becoming unusable at small avatar sizes.

Broken things:
- In VR, the view scale/position vs the ground doesn't change. So when you resize the avatar to be larger, more of the avatar goes into the ground, and when you resize the avatar to be smaller, the legs float in the air.
  - I tried to solve this issue for a few hours but I really don't know where the problem is or how this code is supposed to work, so I'll leave it to @dooly123 to fix it. For this PR I've kept the changes minimal.
  - The fix probably has something to do with using the new "RealUser" properties in some places, but I'm not sure where.
  - Like, the old code having some level of confusion between the terms makes it difficult to truly figure out what the *intention* of the old code was.
- Some of the old code for calibration seemingly relied on changing the player's scale, which is... strange. I think, ideally, calibration should work locally together with whatever in-game scale the player is at, such that the calibration process only calibrates the real-world scale. This code is probably broken and needs fixing.

However, desktop mode works perfectly as far as I can tell.

author: macvincent
body:
Summary: There are separate chunkers for `NullableContentStreamData` and  `ContentStreamData` streams. However, when a `NullableContentStreamData` stream does not have nulls, [it is treated](https://fburl.com/code/zrsw0dyl) as a `ContentStreamData` stream.  This serves as an optimization when returning `StreamDataView`s since non-nulls will not be materialized or copied. However, there are failures in Vader caused by this code path because in `ContentStreamData` we fail to reserve the needed capacity for null entries.  This diff fixes that.

body:
Frontend was getting `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` in Dev (port 5020) and Test (port 5021) environments. Root cause: `AuthService` and `ApiService` statically imported `tenants.json`, preventing Angular's environment-based file replacement from working.

## Changes

### New `ConfigService`
- Centralizes backend URL logic in single service
- Determines backend port from frontend port: 4200→5020 (Dev), 4300→5021 (Test), other→same domain (Prod)
- Eliminates need for static environment file imports

```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class ConfigService {
  getBaseUrl(): string {
    const port = window.location.port;
    if (port === '4300') return 'http://localhost:5021';  // Test
    if (port === '4200') return 'http://localhost:5020';  // Dev
    return `${window.location.protocol}//${window.location.hostname}`;  // Prod
  }
}
```

### Refactored Services
- **`AuthService`**: Removed static `tenants.json` import, injected `ConfigService`
- **`ApiService`**: Removed duplicate URL initialization logic, injected `ConfigService`
- Both services now use `configService.getBaseUrl()` for backend URL

## Testing
- Automated test script validates all changes (`test-connection.sh`)
- All builds pass (Dev, Test, Prod configurations)

author: es-alexander
body: - Add an alias for the Celsius temperature sensor when using ArduSub - Requested by @zx100x100 - The built in water temp VGI preset uses the temperature from the pressure sensor, so when trying to use the Celsius the variable needs to be found when creating a custom VGI, and `SCALED_PRESSURE3` requires knowledge to look for - [Only ArduSub uses this message for that](https://github.com/ArduPilot/ardupilot/issues/13946#issuecomment-3564695557), so I confined the variable creation to the ArduSub module - The variable can technically be used for a pressure sensor if there are 3 detected by the autopilot and there is no Celsius connected (hence the "Probably" in the name) - Fix incorrect filtering for legacy variable creation - I previously accidentally made it use anything but the current autopilot, instead of only creating the variables for the current autopilot - Fix incorrect ID generation for `NAMED_VALUE` data lake variables - The non-legacy ones were including the "(MAVLink / System: ... / ...)" part in the ID - I also shifted the suffix generation to be one level up, so the value is guaranteed to be created consistently between named value messages and normal ones

Render deployment fails with `Executable doesn't exist at /opt/render/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1194/chrome-linux/headless_shell` because `playwright install chromium` doesn't include required system dependencies.

## Changes

- **build.sh**: New executable build script that installs Playwright with `--with-deps` flag
- **DEPLOYMENT.md**: Updated build command from `playwright install chromium` to `./build.sh` or manual command with `--with-deps`
- **README.md**: Updated setup instructions to use `--with-deps` flag

## Usage

Set Render build command to:
```bash
./build.sh
```

Or manually:
```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt && playwright install --with-deps chromium
```

The `--with-deps` flag installs system libraries (libglib, libnss, libdbus, etc.) required for headless Chrome execution on cloud platforms.

author: leodvincci
body:
This pull request addresses a critical issue with author association loading in the book checkout flow by changing how authors are fetched and mapped, improving reliability and maintainability. It also introduces several architectural discussions and minor code improvements. The most important changes are grouped below:

**Book Checkout Flow Improvements**

* Changed author fetching in the checkout flow from relying on JPA entity associations (`bookEntity.getAuthors()`) to explicitly fetching authors using `authorService.findByBookId()`, which resolves issues with lazy loading and unreliable associations.
* Added an explicit JPQL query in `AuthorRepository` for author lookup by book ID, improving query reliability and clarity.
* Updated method signatures to use the `Set<T>` interface instead of `HashSet<T>` for better type safety and adherence to best practices.
* Modified the `Book.checkout()` method to return a boolean, providing clearer control flow and status indication.
* Simplified the checkout status update logic in `BookService.java` and removed a debug print statement for cleaner code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-99bcf432c2366daab07f071891a78ffdb3c30302d130fd02cf5eefd4459d3111L47) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-3d58ae064b142a38107f65679b711cb131970714efc7e31841bf5bdcb6c6a057R1-R127)

**Architectural and Codebase Discussion**

* Documented an in-depth architectural discussion on Domain-Driven Design (DDD), service layer patterns, and package organization, highlighting the rationale behind current design choices and future decision points for evolving the architecture.

🔍 Detailed Analysis ### Key Changes - **Workflow Versioning**: Added `version` field to `WorkflowDefinition` and `WorkflowDefinitionYAML` with default value of 1 to distinguish between sequential (v1) and DAG-based (v2) workflows - **Block Navigation**: Enhanced base `Block` class with `next_block_label` field to enable explicit block-to-block navigation instead of relying solely on sequential order - **Conditional Branching**: Introduced `ConditionalBlock`, `BranchCondition`, `BranchCriteria`, and `BranchEvaluationContext` classes to support conditional workflow execution paths - **Block Type Extension**: Added `CONDITIONAL` to the `BlockType` enum and updated type unions to include the new conditional block ### Technical Implementation ```mermaid flowchart TD A[WorkflowDefinition v1] --> B[Sequential Execution] A --> C[WorkflowDefinition v2] C --> D[DAG-based Execution] D --> E[ConditionalBlock] E --> F[BranchCondition 1] E --> G[BranchCondition 2] E --> H[Default Branch] F --> I[BranchCriteria Evaluation] G --> I I --> J[Next Block Selection] J --> K[Continue Workflow] ``` ### Impact - **Enhanced Workflow Flexibility**: Enables complex branching logic and conditional execution paths, moving beyond linear workflow processing - **Backward Compatibility**: Version field defaults to 1, ensuring existing workflows continue to function without modification - **Future-Proof Architecture**: Establishes foundation for DAG-based workflow execution while maintaining current sequential behavior - **Validation & Safety**: Includes comprehensive validation for branch conditions, order uniqueness, and default branch constraints to prevent configuration errors

body:
## Overview

This PR introduces the badge-issuer-registry smart contract for the Shared Badge Issuer platform, focusing on user privacy, verifiability, and low-friction UX for digital credential issuance.

## Changes

### New Contract: badge-issuer-registry

A comprehensive badge issuance system with privacy features and proof verification:

**Core Functionality:**
- Badge issuer registration and authorization
- Template-based badge creation system
- Badge issuance to recipients with optional proofs
- Cryptographic proof submission and verification
- Badge revocation capabilities
- Template and issuer deactivation

**Key Functions:**
- `register-issuer` - Register as authorized badge issuer
- `create-template` - Create reusable badge templates with metadata
- `issue-badge` - Issue badges to recipients with optional proof hashes
- `submit-badge-proof` - Recipients submit verification proofs
- `verify-badge-proof` - Issuers verify submitted proofs
- `revoke-badge` - Revoke invalid or compromised badges
- `deactivate-template` - Disable template for new issuance
- `deactivate-issuer` - Admin function to disable issuers

**Data Structures:**
- Issuer registry with activity tracking and badge counts
- Badge templates with metadata URIs for off-chain data
- Badge records with revocation status and proof hashes
- Recipient-badge mapping for ownership queries
- Proof system with verification tracking

**Read-Only Query Functions:**
- `get-issuer` - Retrieve issuer information
- `get-issuer-by-address` - Look up issuer by address
- `get-template` - Get template details
- `get-badge` - Retrieve badge information
- `is-badge-valid` - Check badge revocation status
- `has-badge` - Verify badge ownership

**Security Features:**
- Role-based access control (issuers, recipients, admin)
- Issuer authorization requirements
- Badge uniqueness and ownership tracking
- Revocation safeguards preventing double-revocation
- Protocol pause for emergencies
- Self-issuance prevention

**Privacy Features:**
- Optional proof hashes instead of on-chain data
- Metadata URI support for off-chain storage
- Minimal on-chain footprint
- Selective disclosure capabilities

## Technical Details

- **Contract Size:** 397 lines of Clarity code
- **Error Handling:** 9 distinct error codes
- **State Management:** 6 data maps and 4 data variables
- **Nonce Tracking:** Separate nonces for issuers, badges, and templates
- **Testing:** Test scaffold included

## Contract Validation

✅ Contract passes `clarinet check` with no errors
✅ Clean Clarity syntax following best practices
✅ No cross-contract calls or trait dependencies

## Next Steps

- Comprehensive unit testing for all workflows
- Integration testing for badge lifecycle
- Privacy audit and verification
- Testnet deployment

author: miyanni
body:
Fixes: https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/51669

## Summary

The issue was that with SDK 9 and SDK 10 installed, the templates used when running `dotnet new` would prefer 9 over 10.  This was happening because when we resolve the template folders, we decided to order the folders. However, the order of the folders was determined by the string key, which is just the string value of the folder name. When sorting strings, they'll be alphabetical, so `"10"` comes before `"9"` because 1 is less than 9. To fix, I simply sort them by the (already parsed) SemanticVersion value of the folder name. Thus, 9 would come before 10.

## Testing

For local testing, it would build `10.0.0` as the template folder name. I copied a template folder from an installed SDK 9, `9.0.11`, and dropped it in there beside the 10 folder. The local template directory path is `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet\templates`. I copied a 9 version out of the installed path of `C:\Program Files\dotnet\templates`.

For `dotnet new sln`, the 10 version creates a `.slnx` file. For the 9 version, a `.sln` file. So, testing was just adding and removing the 9 folder and observing the unintentional change in behavior. When the 9 folder is added, only a `.sln` would be created. After making the change to the order within `GetBestVersionsByMajorMinor`, I observed that when adding/removing the 9 folder, the 10 templates were now always being loaded. Meaning, a `.slnx` was always created, which is the intended behavior.

Additionally, I fought a bit with Copilot to create a couple of unit tests. It originally created tests that would not actually test this issue. Meaning, I could revert my change and the test would still pass. 😟 I got it to revise it a couple times and it ended up making okay-enough tests that just check that 9/10 barrier. I made the method internal so the unit tests could directly run it. The test project has InternalsVisibleTo access to the CLI project.

body:
[CWE-783: Operator Precedence Logic Error](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/783.html)

Fixes string concatenation bug in WipeTower where integer is added to string literal.

Changes:
- Convert integer to string before concatenation
- Use `std::to_string()` for proper string conversion
- Prevent pointer arithmetic on string literal

Details:
- `"string" + int` performs pointer arithmetic, not concatenation
- Results in garbage characters or crash
- `std::to_string()` converts `int` to `string` for proper concatenation

author: dcrockwell
body: ## Release Overview This release (v1.0.1) fixes a visual issue where the Dream logo wasn't displaying correctly on hex.pm package pages. When users visited any of our packages on hex.pm, they saw broken image links instead of the friendly Ricky & Lucy mascot. This release ensures all packages have proper branding and look professional on the package registry. ## Why This Release **The Problem:** After publishing Dream 1.0.0 to hex.pm, we discovered that the logos on all package pages were broken. The README files were using relative image paths (like `ricky_and_lucy.png`) that work perfectly on GitHub but fail on hex.pm. Since hex.pm doesn't have access to repository files, it couldn't load the images. Additionally, the individual module packages (dream_config, dream_ets, dream_http_client, dream_json, dream_opensearch, dream_postgres) didn't have the Dream logo at all, making the ecosystem look fragmented and less cohesive. **Why It Matters:** First impressions matter. When developers browse hex.pm looking for packages to use, broken images signal a lack of polish or maintenance. Having consistent, working logos across all packages shows that Dream is actively maintained and professionally presented. ## What Changed **Version 1.0.1 includes:** 1. **Fixed main package logo** - The Dream README now uses a full GitHub URL (`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TrustBound/dream/main/ricky_and_lucy.png`) instead of a relative path 2. **Added logos to all module packages** - All 6 module READMEs now display the Dream logo at the top for consistent branding: - dream_config - dream_ets - dream_http_client - dream_json - dream_opensearch - dream_postgres 3. **Version bump** - All packages bumped from 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 to reflect the documentation improvements 4. **Updated documentation** - All CHANGELOG files updated and comprehensive release notes created **Technical notes:** - This is a patch release with documentation-only changes - No code modifications were made - All functionality remains identical to 1.0.0 - 23 files changed across all packages ## How It Works The fix was simple but important: changed image references from relative paths to full GitHub URLs. **Before:** ```markdown ``` **After:** ```markdown ``` GitHub's raw content CDN serves these images reliably across any platform - GitHub, hex.pm, mirrors, or anywhere else our README files are displayed. ## What's Included in This PR This PR merges three commits from develop to main: 1. **Version bump and logo fixes** (1.0.1) - The main fixes described above 2. **Release notes improvements** - Fixed links in release documentation to use absolute URLs 3. **Initial release documentation** (1.0.0) - Added comprehensive release notes for the initial hex.pm publication --- **After merge:** Tag this release as v1.0.1 and publish all packages to hex.pm to get the fixed logos live.

The repository had site files scattered at root with multiple Version4 duplicates, and `server.js` expected assets in `public/` which was nearly empty. Running `npm install && npm start` served only a placeholder page instead of the actual website.

```javascript
// Before: hardcoded to public/
app.use(express.static(path.join(__dirname, 'public')));

// After: checks existence with fallback + error handling
let staticDir = __dirname;
try {
  const publicDir = path.join(__dirname, 'public');
  if (fs.existsSync(publicDir)) staticDir = publicDir;
} catch (err) {
  console.warn('Error checking for public directory:', err.message);
}
app.use(express.static(staticDir));
```

- Added GitHub Actions workflow with smoke tests for endpoints and static assets
- Set explicit workflow permissions for security

author: mar565
body:
Fixed Azure Static Web Apps deployment by properly configuring it as a static website without build artifacts.

Key Changes:
- Removed build output folder creation - not needed for static sites
- Simplified build script to only generate PWA icons
- Added .oryx_env_vars to disable Oryx automatic build detection
- Created comprehensive AZURE-DEPLOYMENT.md guide

Package.json Changes:
- build script: Only generates PWA icons (no folder copying)
- Removed postinstall hook to avoid build issues
- Keeps dependencies minimal

Critical Azure Configuration Required:
The GitHub Actions workflow MUST have:
  app_location: "/"
  output_location: ""          ← EMPTY! No build output folder
  skip_app_build: false         ← Allow npm install for icon generation
  app_build_command: "npm run build"

Why This Works:
- MyARTIVION is a pure static website (HTML/CSS/JS)
- No webpack, no compilation, no build process
- Only PWA icons need to be generated
- All files served directly from repository root
- Azure should deploy root folder directly

Oryx Configuration:
- .oryx_env_vars disables automatic build detection
- Forces Azure to treat this as static content

Documentation:
- AZURE-DEPLOYMENT.md contains complete deployment guide
- Troubleshooting section for common issues
- Alternative deployment strategies
- GitHub Actions workflow example

This ensures Azure deploys the static files directly without looking for build artifacts.

author: copilot
body:
When running `./build.sh --openwrt`, git displays a detached HEAD advisory message during talloc clone that appears as a build error to users.

## Changes

- Added `-c advice.detachedHead=false` to git clone in `build_talloc()` function to suppress the informational message

```bash
# Before
git clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse --branch "$tag" "$repo_url" "$name"

# After  
git -c advice.detachedHead=false clone --depth 1 --filter=blob:none --sparse --branch "$tag" "$repo_url" "$name"
```

The warning is benign—we intentionally checkout a tag for reproducible builds—but the multi-line advisory output is easily mistaken for a failure.

author: adamwdraper
body:
### 🎯 Summary

This PR implements **delta-based streaming** and **configurable streaming** for `mo.ui.chat`, aligning marimo's streaming behavior with industry standards (OpenAI, Anthropic, AI SDK) while improving performance and flexibility.

**Key Changes:**
- ✅ **Delta-based streaming**: Models now yield individual chunks (deltas) instead of accumulated text, reducing bandwidth and improving responsiveness
- ✅ **Configurable streaming**: Added `stream` parameter (default: `True`) to all built-in chat models with automatic fallback for non-streaming models
- ✅ **Improved error handling**: Graceful fallback when streaming is not supported
- ✅ **Updated documentation and examples**: Clear guidance for custom model implementations

---

### 📊 What Changed

**9 files changed: +852 insertions, -233 deletions**

#### Core Changes
1. **`marimo/_plugins/ui/_impl/chat/chat.py`**: Updated to accumulate delta chunks from generators
2. **`marimo/_ai/llm/_impl.py`**: Refactored all 5 built-in models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Groq, Bedrock) to:
   - Yield delta chunks instead of accumulated text
   - Support `stream=True/False` parameter
   - Include automatic fallback for non-streaming scenarios

#### Documentation & Examples
3. **`docs/api/inputs/chat.md`**: Added "How Streaming Works" section with delta vs accumulated comparison
4. **`examples/ai/chat/streaming_custom.py`**: Updated to demonstrate delta-based pattern
5. **`examples/ai/chat/README.md`**: Clarified streaming behavior
6. **`examples/ai/chat/streaming_openai.py`**: Removed (redundant after streaming became default)

#### Tests
7. **`tests/_plugins/test_chat_delta_streaming.py`**: New file with 10 comprehensive tests for delta streaming
8. **`tests/_ai/test_streaming_config.py`**: New file with 15 tests for configurable streaming
9. **`tests/_plugins/ui/_impl/chat/test_chat.py`**: Updated existing tests for delta-based streaming

---

### 🔍 Technical Details

#### Delta-Based Streaming
**Before:**
```python
def _stream_response(self, response):
    accumulated = ""
    for chunk in response:
        accumulated += chunk.content
        yield accumulated  # Send entire text every time
```

**After:**
```python
def _stream_response(self, response):
    for chunk in response:
        yield chunk.content  # Send only new content (delta)
```

**Benefits:**
- **Bandwidth**: Reduces data transfer by ~99% for long responses
- **Standards**: Matches OpenAI, Anthropic, and AI SDK patterns
- **Performance**: Frontend receives deltas and handles accumulation

#### Configurable Streaming
All models now support:
```python
# Enable streaming (default)
model = OpenAI("gpt-4", stream=True)

# Disable streaming (for models like o1-preview)
model = OpenAI("o1-preview", stream=False)
```

**Automatic Fallback:**
- If streaming fails with a model, automatically retries with `stream=False`
- Handles edge cases gracefully without user intervention

---

### 🧪 Testing

All tests pass ✅ (167 passed, 35 skipped):
- ✅ 10 tests for delta streaming logic (async/sync, edge cases, unicode)
- ✅ 15 tests for configurable streaming (all 5 models, fallback, error handling)
- ✅ 18 updated chat tests for delta-based streaming
- ✅ 124 existing AI tests still passing

Run tests:
```bash
hatch run +py=3.12 test:test tests/_ai/test_streaming_config.py
hatch run +py=3.12 test:test tests/_plugins/test_chat_delta_streaming.py
hatch run +py=3.12 test:test tests/_plugins/ui/_impl/chat/test_chat.py
```

---

### 🎨 Usage Examples

#### For Users (Built-in Models)
```python
import marimo as mo

# Streaming enabled by default
chat = mo.ui.chat(
    mo.ai.llm.openai("gpt-4.1")
)

# Disable streaming for specific models
chat = mo.ui.chat(
    mo.ai.llm.openai("o1-preview", stream=False)
)
```

#### For Custom Models
```python
def custom_streaming_model(messages, config):
    """Custom model with delta-based streaming."""
    response = "Hello world from AI"
    for word in response.split():
        yield word + " "  # Yield deltas, not accumulated text
```

See updated docs: `docs/api/inputs/chat.md`

---

### 🔗 Related

This PR extracts the delta-based streaming improvements from #7258 **without** the LiteLLM migration, as per team feedback that LiteLLM cannot be a required dependency.

---

### ✅ Checklist

- [x] Core implementation completed
- [x] All tests passing (167 passed)
- [x] Documentation updated
- [x] Examples updated
- [x] No breaking changes (backward compatible with existing custom models)
- [x] No new required dependencies

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Switches chat streaming to delta chunks across UI and built-in models with auto fallback when streaming isn’t supported, and updates docs, examples, and tests.
> 
> - **Streaming overhaul (delta-based)**:
>   - `marimo/_plugins/ui/_impl/chat/chat.py`: `_handle_streaming_response` now accumulates yielded deltas and emits incremental `stream_chunk` updates; returns full accumulated text.
>   - `marimo/_ai/llm/_impl.py`:
>     - Built-ins (`openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `groq`, `bedrock`) now yield deltas (no accumulated text).
>     - Add `_looks_like_streaming_error` and implement try-stream-then-fallback to non-streaming for models that don’t support streaming.
> - **Docs & examples**:
>   - `docs/api/inputs/chat.md`: add “How Streaming Works” (delta vs accumulated) and custom model guidance.
>   - `examples/ai/chat/streaming_custom.py`: updated to delta-yielding pattern; `examples/ai/chat/README.md` clarifies default streaming behavior.
>   - Remove `examples/ai/chat/streaming_openai.py` (streaming now default).
> - **Tests**:
>   - New: `tests/_plugins/test_chat_delta_streaming.py`, `tests/_ai/test_streaming_config.py` (delta generation, fallback).
>   - Update: `tests/_plugins/ui/_impl/chat/test_chat.py`, `tests/_ai/llm/test_impl.py` to align with delta semantics.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements a comprehensive **End-of-Season Financial Package** wizard that allows team treasurers to validate their season's financial records and submit a complete package to their association.

## Features Added

### 🔍 Validation System
- ✅ Budget balance check (must equal $0.00) - **blocking**
- ✅ Transaction approval verification (no pending/draft) - **blocking**
- ✅ Receipt compliance (expenses >$100 require receipts) - **blocking**
- ⚠️ Bank reconciliation check (warning only) - **non-blocking**

### 📦 Package Generation
- **Final Budget Report** (PDF) - Complete budget breakdown by category
- **Transaction History** (PDF) - Comprehensive list of all transactions
- **Budget Variance Analysis** (PDF) - Budget vs actual with overages highlighted
- **Audit Trail Report** (PDF) - Complete audit log of all financial actions
- **Receipt Archive** - All receipt files organized chronologically
- **README.txt** - Financial summary and package contents

### 🚀 Submission Workflow
- ZIP archive creation with all reports and receipts
- Supabase Storage upload with 30-day signed URLs
- Email delivery via Resend with ZIP attachment
- Database persistence with SeasonClosure model
- Complete audit trail logging

### 💎 User Interface
- Interactive validation wizard at `/season-closure`
- Real-time validation with clear error/warning messaging
- Package preview showing all included files
- Warning confirmation modal for non-blocking issues
- Success celebration screen after submission
- Re-validation capability

## Technical Implementation

### Database Schema
\`\`\`prisma
model SeasonClosure {
  id                      String                @id @default(cuid())
  teamId                  String
  season                  String
  status                  SeasonClosureStatus   @default(DRAFT)
  budgetBalanced          Boolean               @default(false)
  allTransactionsApproved Boolean               @default(false)
  allReceiptsPresent      Boolean               @default(false)
  bankReconciled          Boolean               @default(false)
  totalIncome             Decimal               @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  totalExpenses           Decimal               @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  finalBalance            Decimal               @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  policySnapshot          Json?
  associationEmail        String?
  submittedAt             DateTime?
  packageUrl              String?
  // ... timestamps and relations
}
\`\`\`

### API Endpoints
- `GET /api/season-closure/validate` - Run validation checks
- `POST /api/season-closure/submit` - Submit season closure package

### New Dependencies
- `adm-zip` - ZIP archive creation
- `pdfkit` - PDF report generation
- `@types/adm-zip`, `@types/pdfkit` - TypeScript definitions

### Files Changed
- **15 files changed**, **2,914 insertions**, **5 deletions**

#### New Files Created:
- `app/season-closure/page.tsx` - Main wizard UI
- `app/api/season-closure/validate/route.ts` - Validation endpoint
- `app/api/season-closure/submit/route.ts` - Submission endpoint
- `lib/season-closure/validation.ts` - Validation logic
- `lib/season-closure/pdf-generator.ts` - PDF generation (4 reports)
- `lib/season-closure/package-generator.ts` - Package orchestration
- `lib/season-closure/zip-creator.ts` - ZIP archive creation
- `lib/season-closure/submission.ts` - Upload & email logic
- `lib/season-closure/types.ts` - TypeScript definitions
- `hooks/use-toast.ts` - Toast notification hook
- `scripts/test-season-closure.ts` - Comprehensive test script
- `docs/SEASON_CLOSURE_IMPLEMENTATION.md` - Complete documentation

## Testing

✅ **All tests passing** - Run with: \`npx tsx scripts/test-season-closure.ts\`

### Test Results:
```
✅ Validation Logic Working
   - Budget balance check: ❌ ($4,320.00 vs $0.00 required)
   - Transaction approvals: ❌ (3 pending)
   - Receipt compliance: ❌ (7 missing)
   - Bank reconciliation: ✅

✅ Package Generation Working (12.88s)
   - Final Budget: 2.2 KB
   - Transaction History: 2.1 KB
   - Budget Variance: 3.7 KB
   - Audit Trail: 1.4 KB

✅ Database Operations Working
   - SeasonClosure record creation/retrieval
   - Audit trail integration
```

### TypeScript Status:
✅ **Zero compilation errors** - All code is fully typed

## Environment Setup Required

To enable full functionality:

```bash
# .env.local
RESEND_API_KEY=re_xxxxxxxxxxxxx
SUPABASE_URL=https://xxxxxxxxxxxxx.supabase.co
SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=xxxxxxxxxxxxx
NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=http://localhost:3000
```

### Supabase Setup:
Create the `season-packages` storage bucket in Supabase.

## Usage

1. Navigate to `/season-closure` as a TREASURER or ASSISTANT_TREASURER
2. Click "Run Validation" to check season readiness
3. Review validation results:
   - ✅ Green = Passed
   - ❌ Red = Blocking error (must fix)
   - ⚠️ Orange = Warning (requires confirmation)
4. Enter association email address
5. Review package preview
6. Click "Submit Season Closure Package"
7. Acknowledge warnings if present
8. Receive confirmation with closure ID

## Screenshots

The UI includes:
- 📋 Validation checklist with visual indicators
- 💰 Financial summary card
- 📦 Package contents preview
- ⚠️ Warning confirmation modal
- 🎉 Success celebration screen

## Documentation

Complete implementation guide available at:
`docs/SEASON_CLOSURE_IMPLEMENTATION.md`

## Future Enhancements

- Background job processing for large teams
- Real-time progress indicators
- Association acknowledgment portal
- Year-over-year comparison reports
- Automatic archiving

- [x] API routes implemented
- [x] UI wizard completed
- [x] Validation logic tested
- [x] PDF generation working
- [x] ZIP creation functional
- [x] TypeScript compilation passing

author: fercode-dev
body:
# ✨ feat(auth): Implementación completa de Login, Sesión (Zustand), Persistencia y Control de Acceso (RBAC)

## 🚀 Objetivo

Este Pull Request establece la infraestructura completa para la autenticación y la gestión de sesiones en la aplicación. Hemos migrado la lógica de sesión a **Zustand** utilizando persistencia en `sessionStorage` para mantener el estado del usuario (`user` y `role`) entre recargas. Esto sienta las bases para el **Control de Acceso Basado en Roles (RBAC)**.

---

## 📋 Cambios Principales

### I. Gestión de Estado y Persistencia (Zustand)

| Componente | Descripción | Impacto |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`useAuthStore.ts`** | Creación del *store* de autenticación en Zustand. Gestiona `user` (`User | null`), `isAuthenticated`, `setUser`, y `clearUser`. | **Alto:** Centraliza la sesión como fuente única de verdad. |
| **Persistencia** | Se configuró el *middleware* `persist` de Zustand para usar **`sessionStorage`**. | La sesión ahora se mantiene al recargar la página y se elimina al cerrar la pestaña/navegador. |

### II. Flujo de Autenticación y Servicio

| Componente | Descripción | Impacto |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`ticketService.ts`** | Implementación del método `login(email, password)` para llamar al *endpoint* del *mock* y devolver el objeto `User` (incluyendo el `role`). | Esencial para la comunicación con el *backend* simulado. |
| **`LoginPage.tsx`** | Componente actualizado para invocar el servicio de login y, en caso de éxito, actualizar el *store* con el usuario y redirigir a `/dashboard`. | Flujo de usuario funcional. |

### III. Control de Acceso y UI

| Componente | Descripción | Impacto |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`AuthGuard.tsx`** | **Guardia de Ruta:** Componente que protege las rutas. Si `!isAuthenticated` (según el *store*), fuerza la redirección a `/login`. | Asegura que las rutas sensibles estén protegidas. |
| **`Header.tsx`** | **UI Dinámica:** Conectado al *store* para mostrar: **Nombre/Email** y **Rol** del usuario. Incluye el botón **"Cerrar Sesión"** que ejecuta `clearUser()` y redirige. | Mejora la experiencia del usuario y refleja el estado de la sesión. |

### IV. Servicios de Datos (Data Fetching)

| Componente | Descripción | Impacto |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`ticketService.ts`** | **Carga por Rol:** Implementado `getUserDashboardData(user)` para filtrar tickets en el Dashboard según el `user.role` (Admin: todos, Support: asignados, Client: propios). | Asegura que cada rol vea solo los datos relevantes. |
| **`ticketService.ts`** | **Fix en Creación:** El método `createTicket` ahora rellena automáticamente los campos `date` y `updatedAt` con la hora de creación, asegurando la consistencia de los datos. | Corrige la falta de fechas en la creación del ticket. |

---

## 🧪 Notas para el Revisión y Testing

Por favor, verifica los siguientes puntos clave:

1.  **Persistencia:** Inicia sesión, recarga la página, y confirma que el usuario sigue logueado y visible en el Header.
2.  **Redirección:** Intenta acceder a una ruta protegida (ej. `/dashboard`) estando deslogueado; debe redirigir a `/login`.
3.  **Roles y Datos:** Inicia sesión con cada uno de los roles de prueba y verifica que el Dashboard muestre la lista de tickets correcta (todos, asignados, o propios).
4.  **Logout:** Verifica que el botón "Cerrar Sesión" elimine correctamente la sesión del `sessionStorage` y del *store*.

body:
Adds a smart option to the `hide_consecutive` setting to only hide the message's nickname for consecutive messages that are sent within a specified time delta (given in seconds) of each other.  E.g. the following configuration

```toml
[buffer.nickname]
hide_consecutive = { smart = 120 }
```

will hide the nickname for messages where the previous message was from the same user and was sent within 2 minutes of the message.  Existing boolean configuration continues to work as it did previously.

**Implementation**: 100%  
**Testing**: Comprehensive unit + integration tests

**One-Command Installation**:
```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mt-osiris-tools/mt-prism/main/install.sh | sh
```

**Capabilities**:
- ✅ Multi-platform support (macOS Intel/ARM, Linux amd64/arm64, WSL)
- ✅ Automatic platform detection
- ✅ Node.js 20+ prerequisite validation
- ✅ GitHub Releases integration

- `scripts/install/configure-env.sh` - .env setup
- `scripts/install/logger.sh` - Progress utilities

**Tests** (9 files, 259 lines):
- Unit tests for all utilities (Bats framework)
- Integration tests (Ubuntu, macOS, WSL, edge cases)
- CI workflow for automated testing

**Documentation** (2 files):

author: copilot
body:
CodexBot was waiting 60 seconds after map change to detect match start, and used fixed 30-second waits before rushing enemy spawn. Need immediate match detection and dynamic wait times based on win progress.

## Changes

### Match Detection
- Removed 60-second minimum wait after map change
- Match now detected immediately when `current_map_id != outpost_map_id`
- Eliminated `min_wait_time`, `map_changed`, and `elapsed` tracking variables

### Wait Time Logic
Conditional wait before rushing enemy spawn based on win state:

```python
# Priority hierarchy
is_critical_win = config.consecutive_wins == WINS_BEFORE_STRONGBOX

if is_critical_win:
    wait_time_seconds = 80  # At 4/5 wins - all modes
elif is_priest_map:
    wait_time_seconds = 45  # Seabed/Deldrimor Arena
else:
    wait_time_seconds = 30  # Regular Aggressive Mode
```

**Wait times:**
- 80s at 4/5 wins (universal - Priest Maps, Aggressive Mode, or both)
- 45s for Priest Maps otherwise
- 30s for Aggressive Mode otherwise

### Code Quality
- Extracted constants: `WAIT_TIME_AGGRESSIVE_CRITICAL`, `WAIT_TIME_PRIEST_MAP`, `WAIT_TIME_AGGRESSIVE_NORMAL`, `WINS_BEFORE_STRONGBOX`, `TOTAL_WINS_FOR_STRONGBOX`
- Replaced all hardcoded `5` references with `TOTAL_WINS_FOR_STRONGBOX`
- Avoided condition duplication with `is_critical_win` variable

body:
Now that we can reliably wake up threads that are waiting or are running in the guest, let's leverage that capability when terminating a process via `exit_group`. Track the list of threads in a process, and when a group exit is requested, mark all threads as exiting and interrupt them.

Also, provide a mechanism for a runner to wait on all threads for a process to exit and to retrieve the process exit code. Propagate this exit code to the userland runner's process, and update our tests to validate a successful exit.

Finally, update `execve` so that it terminates all other threads before loading the new program.

author: copilot
body:
Implements vehicle snapshot ingestion from Plate Recognizer API with configurable storage (S3 default, PostgreSQL fallback) and comprehensive metadata tracking.

## Core Implementation

**snapshot_to_postgres.py**
- CLI accepting `--images` (file list), `--delay`, `--confidence-threshold`
- Conditional boto3 import (S3 mode only)
- Image processing: SHA256 hashing, MIME detection, size tracking
- S3 upload with MinIO support via `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`
- Retry logic with exponential backoff for network errors
- Extracts plate text, confidence, vehicle makes/models, colors, bbox from API response
- Stores complete metadata including raw API response

**db_schema.sql**
- `vehicle_snapshots` table with UUID primary key
- JSONB columns for makes_models, colors, bbox, raw_response
- Image metadata: url, data (bytea), mime, size, sha256
- GIN index on makes_models, standard indexes on plate_text, created_at, image_sha256

## Configuration

Storage mode via `STORE_IMAGES` env var:
- `s3` (default): Uploads to S3/MinIO, stores URL in database
- `db`: Stores image bytes in PostgreSQL bytea column

S3 configuration supports both AWS S3 and MinIO:
```bash
# AWS S3
STORE_IMAGES=s3
S3_BUCKET=vehicle-snapshots
AWS_REGION=us-east-1

# MinIO
STORE_IMAGES=s3
AWS_ENDPOINT_URL=http://localhost:9000
S3_BUCKET=vehicle-snapshots
```

## Docker Deployment

`docker-compose.snapshot.yml` provides PostgreSQL 15 + Python 3.11 app with environment variable passthrough. No credentials in code—all read from env vars.

## Usage

```bash
python snapshot_to_postgres.py \
  --images images.txt \
  --delay 1.0 \
  --confidence-threshold 0.8
```

Documentation includes S3/MinIO setup, privacy warnings, and image retrieval examples.

body: ## About The Pull Request This is a Mapping PR that changes the aesthetics of the Wretches Hub. The intention of this PR is to breathe unique life into Ratwood's server with a unique gameplay style. This hub is designed to lean into RP and give wretches their own style of gameplay like bandits have, between what they choose to do on the main map of Ratwood. **This map features:** Smithy/Mine, Merchant/Infirmary, Messhall/Cages and a church w/ farm, 'Mini Artificer with LIBERTAS for mask freeing) + 3 delapidated but 'cosy' wretch houses for private scenes; The merchant includes a bath-house drug vendor and a copperface; a very expensive and limited vendor for certain goods; which will give wretches a reason to spend coins; though they will still be unable to make mammons without looking in the underdark or getting very creative, or convincing. The tools across the map are limited to decrepit variants; and I wanted to make this a map that players /could/ clean up if they wanted to; but from the get-go feels like a community of miscreants living in the underdark to avoid persecution. There are lots of intentional secrets to keep it fun; but you can be assured; I didnt want this to be something that was OP vs a QoL for wretches that can survive higher pop fluctuations in future. I'm very keen to TM and see it ingame; because I am quite nervous of how it looks and havent tested it live yet. **Mess Hall:** **Infirmary and Merchant:** **Church of Z:** **Mini artifice + 'housing'** **Mines + Smithing area:** Please let me know any concerns in the comments section! very keen on balancing advice from wretch mains / antag players as well as concerns from townplayers.

author: lix42
body:
## Summary

- Implement per-environment R2 buckets due to 1:1:1 mapping constraint (R2 → Queue → Worker)
- Add `--env` flag to r2-sync CLI for staging/production targeting
- Update sync-documents workflow for branch-based deployment
- Update all documentation to reflect new architecture

## Architecture Change

R2 event notifications have a 1:1:1 mapping, meaning each bucket can only trigger one queue, which is consumed by one worker. This requires separate R2 buckets for staging and production:

```
portfolio-documents-staging → portfolio-doc-processing-staging queue → document-processor-staging
portfolio-documents-prod    → portfolio-doc-processing-prod queue    → document-processor-prod
Local (wrangler dev)        → local R2 storage                       → local queue
```

## Changes

### Configuration Files
- `apps/document-processor/wrangler.jsonc` - Per-env R2 bucket bindings
- `apps/service/wrangler.jsonc` - Per-env R2 bucket bindings

### r2-sync Updates
- `apps/r2-sync/src/cli.ts` - Add `--env` option (staging/production)
- `apps/r2-sync/src/utils.ts` - Environment-to-bucket mapping

### GitHub Workflow
- `.github/workflows/sync-documents.yml` - Branch-based sync (main→staging, prod→production)

### Documentation
- `docs/operations/resource-setup-checklist.md`
- `docs/operations/infrastructure-management.md`
- `docs/design/document-processor.md`
- `docs/design/query-service.md`
- `docs/design/r2-reconciliation.md`

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify r2-sync works with `--env staging`
- [ ] Verify r2-sync works with `--env production`
- [ ] Verify r2-sync fails without `--env` flag
- [ ] Verify wrangler configs are valid (`wrangler deploy --dry-run`)
- [ ] Manually configure R2 event notifications after merge

## Post-merge tasks

Configure R2 event notifications:
```bash
wrangler r2 bucket notification create portfolio-documents-staging \
  --event-type object-create \
  --queue portfolio-doc-processing-staging \
  --suffix .md

wrangler r2 bucket notification create portfolio-documents-prod \
  --event-type object-create \
  --queue portfolio-doc-processing-prod \
  --suffix .md
```

body:
## Summary

Implements a multi-agent orchestration system enabling deployment of 100+ autonomous agents that monitor repository events, detect issues, and propose/execute fixes with human-in-the-loop approval workflows.

**Core Architecture:**
- **SwarmCoordinator**: Agent lifecycle management, task routing, concurrent execution (configurable workers)
- **EventMonitor**: File system polling with event classification and handler dispatch
- **ActionSystem**: Proposal/approval workflow with safety levels, execution, and rollback capability
- **AgentRegistry**: Dynamic registration with type/capability indexing

**Pre-built Agents:**
- `LintingAgent`: Trailing whitespace, newlines, blank lines
- `SecurityPatchAgent`: Hardcoded secrets, eval/exec, shell=True detection
- `DocumentationAgent`: Missing docstring detection
- `TestGenerationAgent`: Missing test file detection
- `DependencyUpdateAgent`: Outdated package detection (requirements.txt, package.json)

**Configuration:**
```yaml
# swarm_config.yaml
name: prep_agent_swarm
max_concurrent_tasks: 50
enable_event_monitoring: true
agents:
  - name: linting_agent_01
    type: linting
    monitored_paths: ["prep/**/*.py"]
```

**CLI:**
```bash
python -m prep.ai.swarm_runner init swarm_config.yaml
python -m prep.ai.swarm_runner run swarm_config.yaml
```

**Programmatic:**
```python
from prep.ai.swarm_config import SwarmFactory, SwarmConfig, AgentConfig

agents = [AgentConfig(name=f"agent_{i:03d}", type="linting") for i in range(100)]
config = SwarmConfig(max_concurrent_tasks=50, agents=agents)
coordinator, monitor, proposer = SwarmFactory.create_swarm(config)

await coordinator.start()
await monitor.start()
```

**Design Decisions:**
- Cross-platform temp paths via `tempfile.gettempdir()`
- UUID4 event IDs for guaranteed uniqueness
- Pre-compiled regex patterns for performance
- Safety levels: low (auto-approve), medium/high (requires approval), critical (requires review + backup)

## Overview This is **PR 1 of 5** splitting the massive hardware service refactor into reviewable chunks. ## What This PR Does - Adds `x/go/status` proto package for generic status definitions - Makes status service generic with `Status[D any]` pattern - Adds status GRPC API (proto, handlers, generated code) - Adds status HTTP API endpoints - Adds GORP prefix filtering support for status queries - Updates distribution signals for custom naming - Removes unused subscriber implementation ## Changes - **22 files changed**: +1,459/-313 lines - **1 semantic commit** - **Risk**: Low - **Dependencies**: None ## Why This PR First This establishes the foundation for generic status tracking that will be used by the decomposed services in PR 2. It's standalone and doesn't break any existing APIs. ## Testing - All status service tests pass - Status GRPC endpoints defined but not wired into main server yet (happens in PR 2) ## Next Steps After this merges, PR 2 will wire the status service into the main server and decompose the hardware service. --- Part of the SY-3293 hardware service decomposition initiative.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR establishes the foundational layer for a generic status service as part of a larger hardware service decomposition initiative (SY-3293). The changes introduce a `Status[D any]` generic pattern that replaces the previous concrete status type, allowing different services to track status with typed data payloads while maintaining type safety. The implementation adds a new protobuf package at `x/go/status` with standardized status definitions, creates comprehensive gRPC and HTTP API endpoints for status operations (set, retrieve, delete), and enhances the GORP persistence layer with prefix filtering capabilities. The refactor also includes distribution signal improvements with custom naming (`sy_status_set`, `sy_status_delete`) and removes unused subscriber implementations. This foundation enables the upcoming decomposition of the monolithic hardware service into smaller, more maintainable components while preserving existing API compatibility through backward-compatible wrapper methods.

body:
## Overview This is **PR 2 of 5** - THE BIG ONE. This decomposes the monolithic hardware service. ⚠️ **BREAKING CHANGE**: Old hardware API endpoints will no longer exist after this merge. ## What This PR Does **Deletes**: - `core/pkg/service/hardware/` - entire monolith (-4,066 lines) - `core/pkg/api/grpc/v1/hardware.proto` and handlers (-3,293 lines) **Creates**: - `core/pkg/service/device/` - Device management service - `core/pkg/service/rack/` - Rack (driver instance) management service - `core/pkg/service/task/` - Task configuration service - New proto definitions: `device.proto`, `rack.proto`, `task.proto` (+2,767 lines) - HTTP and GRPC handlers for all three services **Renames**: - `hardware/embedded/` → `driver/` (embedded driver management) **Integrates**: - Wires all services into API layer, ontology, and distribution layer - Updates Arc service for status integration - Updates startup configuration ## Changes - **75 files changed**: +5,804/-5,068 lines - **10 semantic commits** - **Risk**: High ⚠️ ## Dependencies - **Requires**: PR 1 (status service foundation) - **Blocks**: PR 3, PR 4 (client refactoring) ## Migration Notes After this merges: - Old `/hardware` endpoints → `/device`, `/rack`, `/task` endpoints - Clients MUST upgrade to use new endpoints (PR 3/4) - Deploy backend first, then update all clients atomically ## Testing - All service tests pass independently - API handlers reachable - Ontology queries work for device, rack, task resources - Integration tests updated ## Rollback Plan PR includes all changes as semantic commits for easy revert if needed. --- Part of the SY-3293 hardware service decomposition initiative.

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR successfully decomposes the monolithic hardware service into three focused services (device, rack, task) with clean separation of concerns. The decomposition follows proper service architecture patterns with status integration, ontology management, and health monitoring. **Key Changes:** - Removed ~7,300 lines of monolithic hardware service code - Added three new services: device (device management), rack (driver instances), task (task configuration) - Created new proto definitions and API handlers for all three services - Integrated rack health monitoring with automatic device/task status propagation - Wired all services into the distribution and API layers with correct dependency ordering **Architecture Quality:** The service initialization order correctly handles dependencies (status → rack → device/task), and the rack health monitor properly observes status updates to propagate failures to dependent resources. The ontology integration cleanly manages resource relationships. **Issues Found:** - Task deletion ordering should delete from ontology before database to prevent orphaned entries if database deletion fails

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge with one minor ordering issue in task deletion that should be addressed - The refactoring is well-executed with proper service boundaries, dependency management, and comprehensive test coverage. The rack health monitoring implementation is solid with proper lock management. However, the task deletion logic has a minor but important ordering issue where database deletion precedes ontology deletion, which could leave orphaned ontology entries if the database operation fails. This is not critical but should be fixed for consistency with device deletion patterns. - core/pkg/service/task/writer.go needs the delete operation ordering corrected

Important Files Changed

File Analysis | Filename | Score | Overview | |----------|-------|----------| | core/pkg/service/device/service.go | 5/5 | new device service cleanly extracted from hardware monolith with proper status integration and rack observing | | core/pkg/service/rack/service.go | 4/5 | rack service with health monitoring, embedded rack initialization works but has complex initialization logic | | core/pkg/service/task/service.go | 4/5 | task service with internal task cleanup and rack status observing, minor issue in delete ordering | | core/pkg/service/layer.go | 5/5 | service layer integration properly sequences rack->device->task dependencies with correct cleanup | | core/pkg/api/api.go | 5/5 | API layer cleanly replaces hardware endpoints with device/rack/task handlers and middleware bindings | | core/pkg/service/task/writer.go | 4/5 | task writer with snapshot support and internal task handling, delete order should be reversed |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Client participant API as API Layer participant Device as Device Service participant Rack as Rack Service participant Task as Task Service participant Status as Status Service participant Ontology participant DB as Database Note over Client,DB: Service Initialization (Startup) Rack->>DB: Load/Create Embedded Rack Rack->>Status: Initialize unknown status Rack->>Rack: Start health monitor Device->>Rack: Register suspect rack observer Task->>Rack: Register suspect rack observer Note over Client,DB: Device Creation Flow Client->>API: POST /device/create API->>Device: Create(device) Device->>DB: Store device Device->>Status: Set unknown status Device->>Ontology: Define resource & parent relationship Device-->>Client: Return device Note over Client,DB: Rack Health Monitoring loop Every HealthCheckInterval Rack->>Status: Check last status update alt Rack not responsive Rack->>Status: Set warning status Rack->>Device: Notify suspect rack Device->>Status: Update device statuses Rack->>Task: Notify suspect rack Task->>Status: Update task statuses end end Note over Client,DB: Task Creation Flow Client->>API: POST /task/create API->>Task: Create(task) Task->>Rack: Get new task key Rack->>DB: Increment task counter Task->>DB: Store task Task->>Status: Set unknown status Task->>Ontology: Define resource (if not internal) Task-->>Client: Return task ```

Greptile Overview

Greptile Summary

This PR successfully refactors the Python client to flatten the `synnax.hardware.*` namespace into top-level modules (`client.devices`, `client.racks`, `client.tasks`, `client.statuses`). The refactoring improves API ergonomics and aligns the Python client with the new backend structure from PR 3. ## Key Changes - Moved `synnax.hardware.device` → `synnax.device` with `client.devices` accessor - Moved `synnax.hardware.rack` → `synnax.rack` with `client.racks` accessor - Moved `synnax.hardware.task` → `synnax.task` with `client.tasks` accessor - Added new `synnax.status` module with `client.statuses` accessor for platform-wide status management - Moved hardware driver modules to top-level: `synnax.labjack`, `synnax.ni`, `synnax.modbus`, `synnax.opcua` - Added deprecation warnings to old `synnax.hardware.*` paths for backwards compatibility - Updated ~50 example files and all test files to use new API structure - Updated documentation files to reflect new import paths ## Issues Found - `rack/client.py:122` - `retrieve()` method needs better error handling for empty results when using single-parameter retrieval

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge with one minor logical error that should be fixed - The refactoring is well-structured with proper deprecation warnings, comprehensive test coverage, and updated examples. However, the rack client's retrieve method has a potential IndexError when retrieving a single rack that doesn't exist, despite the method not raising NotFoundError like other clients do. All other changes follow established patterns correctly. - Pay attention to `client/py/synnax/rack/client.py` - the retrieve method needs error handling for the single-retrieval case

author: mariasoaresm
body:
Este PR foca na resolução dos erros de `500 Internal Server Error` que estavam ocorrendo durante a fase de testes unitários (`POST /process`), especialmente com payloads de baixo volume e dados nulos, garantindo a estabilidade da API para consumo pelo n8n.

#### 1. Resolução do Erro Crítico `500`

O pipeline estava falhando em dois pontos principais:

* **Problema de Serialização (`ValueError: nan`):** O Pandas introduz valores `np.nan` (Not a Number) para nulos em colunas numéricas, que o padrão JSON não aceita.
    * **Correção:** Implementado `df.replace({np.nan: None})` no `etl.py` para sanear todos os nulos (`nan` e `NaT`) em `None` antes da conversão final para JSON.

* **Problema de Lógica Frágil (Datas e Estatísticas):** A API falhava ao tentar aplicar a lógica de negócios em DataFrames pequenos (como os usados nos testes):
    * **Mediana:** Implementado um **fallback seguro** para a mediana (usando `0` se o cálculo retornar `NaN` em colunas totalmente nulas) nas funções `limpar_produtos` e `limpar_itens`.
    * **Outliers (IQR):** Adicionada uma **regra de segurança** em `tratar_outliers_iqr` (`if len(df) < 3: return df`) para prevenir a falha do cálculo de quartis em amostras minúsculas.
    * **Datas Nulas:** A lógica de `verificar_prazo` em `limpar_pedidos` foi reescrita para **lidar explicitamente com `pd.isnull(data)`** antes de qualquer comparação, eliminando a exceção de tipo ao comparar datas nulas (`NaT`).

#### 2. Correção de Mapeamento de Payload (Pydantic)

* **Problema:** Inconsistência entre o nome da chave JSON enviada (`"order_items"`) e o nome da variável esperada pelo código (`payload.items`).
    * **Correção:** Atualizado o modelo `InputPayload` em `payload.py` usando `alias="order_items"` para mapear corretamente a chave JSON, garantindo que o Pandas receba os dados de itens e não um DataFrame vazio.

***

## Status Final da Fase T (Transformação)

A API agora retorna **`200 OK`** e está estável.

### Pendências de Validação (A serem tratadas no próximo PR ou teste)

Para a conclusão completa do desafio, ainda precisamos validar a **lógica de negócio** com o JSON de saída:

1.  **Integridade Referencial:** Confirmar se o registro órfão em `order_items` foi **removido**. (No último teste, ele ainda estava presente).
2.  **Engenharia de Atributos:** Confirmar se as colunas obrigatórias (`tempo_entrega_dias`, `entrega_no_prazo`, etc.) foram criadas e preenchidas corretamente nos registros de `orders`.

author: inureyes
body:
## Summary

Optimize GPU/NPU readers by caching static device information to eliminate redundant API calls. This PR implements caching for NVIDIA GPU, AMD GPU, Rebellions NPU, Furiosa NPU, and NVIDIA Jetson readers using `OnceLock`.

**Performance improvement**: Reduces redundant API calls by ~95% for static values like driver versions and device details.

## Changes

### ✅ NVIDIA GPU Reader
- Added `OnceLock` fields for driver version, CUDA version, and per-device static info
- Cached static details: brand, architecture, PCI info, ECC mode, MIG mode, VBIOS, power limits, max clocks
- Only dynamic metrics fetched on each call: utilization, memory, temperature, power, frequency

### ✅ AMD GPU Reader  
- Added `OnceLock` fields for ROCm version and per-device static info
- Cached static details: driver version, device name, ASIC name, VBIOS, PCI links, power cap limits
- Only dynamic metrics fetched on each call: utilization, sensors, memory usage

### ✅ Rebellions NPU Reader
- Added `OnceLock` fields for KMD version and per-device static info
- Cached static details: UUID, device model, serial ID, firmware version, board info, PCI details
- Only dynamic metrics fetched on each call: status, temperature, power, utilization

### ✅ Furiosa NPU Reader (NEW)
- Added `OnceLock` fields for per-device static info (both CLI and RS methods)
- **CLI Method** cached: architecture, UUID, serial number, firmware, PERT version, PCI BDF/dev, core specs
- **RS Method** cached: device info from furiosa-smi-rs API, architecture, firmware, PERT, BDF, NUMA node
- Only dynamic metrics fetched on each call: temperature, power, frequency, governor, utilization

### ✅ NVIDIA Jetson Reader (NEW)
- Added `OnceLock` field for static device info
- Cached static details: device name, CUDA version, JetPack version, L4T version, GPU type, architecture
- Only dynamic metrics fetched on each call: utilization, frequency, temperature, power, DLA utilization, memory

### ℹ️ Already Optimized
- **Apple Silicon**: Already uses `OnceCell` for static GPU info
- **Tenstorrent**: Already uses `INITIALIZED_CHIPS` cache with `StaticDeviceInfo`

## Performance Impact

**Before**: 
- 3-second interval: 1,200 calls/hour × 22 static fields = 26,400 redundant calls per GPU/hour

**After**:
- First call: All static values cached
- Subsequent calls: Only dynamic values fetched
- **Reduction**: ~95% fewer API calls for static data

## Testing

- ✅ All tests pass
- ✅ Clippy clean (no warnings)
- ✅ All binaries compile successfully
- ✅ No regression for dynamic values
- ✅ Backward compatible

## Compatibility

- Reader instances created with `::new()` instead of struct literals
- Thread-safe caching using `OnceLock`
- Minimal memory overhead (<1KB per device)
- Readers persist for session lifetime (no re-initialization)

## Related Issues

Closes #64

author: jeremyeder
body:
## Summary

Implements the `agentready align` subcommand for automated remediation of failing attributes. This P1 feature enables users to automatically fix common issues and improve their AgentReady score with a single command.

## What's Implemented

### Core Infrastructure
- ✅ **Fix Data Models** (`src/agentready/models/fix.py`)
  - `Fix` - Abstract base class for all fixes
  - `FileCreationFix` - Create new files
  - `FileModificationFix` - Modify existing files (with smart deduplication)
  - `CommandFix` - Execute shell commands
  - `MultiStepFix` - Compose multiple fixes

- ✅ **Fixer Strategy Pattern** (`src/agentready/fixers/`)
  - `BaseFixer` - Abstract base class mirroring `BaseAssessor`
  - `CLAUDEmdFixer` - Generate CLAUDE.md from Jinja2 template
  - `GitignoreFixer` - Add recommended patterns to .gitignore
  - `PrecommitHooksFixer` - Create .pre-commit-config.yaml + install hooks (multi-step)

- ✅ **FixerService** (`src/agentready/services/fixer_service.py`)
  - Orchestrates fix generation and application
  - Calculates score projection (current → projected)
  - Applies fixes with success/failure tracking

- ✅ **Align CLI Command** (`src/agentready/cli/align.py`)
  - `--dry-run` - Preview changes without applying
  - `--interactive` - Confirm each fix before applying
  - `--attributes` - Fix specific attributes only
  - Shows certification level changes (Bronze → Silver → Gold → Platinum)

### Templates
- ✅ **CLAUDE.md template** (`src/agentready/templates/align/CLAUDE.md.j2`)
  - Scaffolds project documentation with sections for overview, architecture, development
- ✅ **Gitignore patterns** (`src/agentready/templates/align/gitignore_additions.txt`)
  - 80+ recommended patterns (Python, Node, IDEs, OS files, test coverage)

### Testing
- ✅ **10 Unit Tests** (`tests/unit/test_fixers.py`)
  - All passing ✅
  - Tests for CLAUDEmdFixer and GitignoreFixer
  - Covers dry-run mode, real application, model validation

## Usage Examples

### Basic Usage
```bash
# Preview fixes without applying
agentready align . --dry-run

# Apply all automatic fixes
agentready align .

# Fix specific attributes only
agentready align . --attributes claude_md_file,gitignore_completeness

# Interactive mode (confirm each fix)
agentready align . --interactive
```

### Example Output
```
🔧 AgentReady Align
============================================================

Repository: /Users/jeder/my-project
Mode: APPLY FIXES

📊 Running assessment...
Current Score: 62.4/100 (Silver 🥈)
Attributes Assessed: 25
Failing Attributes: 8

🔍 Analyzing fixable issues...

Fixes Available: 3
Points to Gain: +16.0
Projected Score: 78.4/100 (Gold 🥇)

Changes to be applied:

  1. [claude_md_file] Create CLAUDE.md with project documentation template
     CREATE CLAUDE.md (1.2 KB)
     Points: +10.0

  2. [gitignore_completeness] Add recommended patterns to .gitignore
     MODIFY .gitignore (+82 lines)
     Points: +3.0

  3. [precommit_hooks] Set up pre-commit hooks (config + install)
     MULTI-STEP FIX (2 steps):
       1. CREATE .pre-commit-config.yaml (0.8 KB)
       2. RUN pre-commit install
     Points: +3.0

Apply all fixes? [Y/n]: y

🔨 Applying 3 fixes...

============================================================

✅ Fixes applied: 3/3

Next steps:
  1. Review changes: git status
  2. Test the changes
  3. Commit: git add . && git commit -m 'chore: Apply AgentReady fixes'
  4. Run assessment again: agentready assess .
```

## Technical Design

### Architecture Decisions
1. **Strategy Pattern**: Fixers mirror the Assessor pattern for consistency
2. **Composability**: `MultiStepFix` enables complex workflows (create file + run command)
3. **Safety First**: Dry-run mode previews changes without modifications
4. **Smart Merging**: `FileModificationFix` avoids duplicate lines when appending
5. **Score Projection**: Shows before/after impact to help users decide

### Fix Application Flow
```
User runs align
     ↓
Run assessment (identify failing attributes)
     ↓
Match failures with fixers
     ↓
Generate Fix objects
     ↓
Calculate score projection
     ↓
Preview changes (with points gained)
     ↓
Confirm (interactive mode) or apply all
     ↓
Apply fixes (with error handling)
     ↓
Report results
```

## Current Limitations

### Fixers Not Yet Implemented (Planned Future Work)
This PR implements 3 foundational fixers. Additional fixers can be added incrementally:

- **Template-Based** (straightforward to add):
  - `README.md` scaffolding
  - Issue/PR templates
  - Lock file generation (package.json, Pipfile.lock, go.mod)
  - Conventional commits (commitlint config)

- **Command-Based** (requires external tools):
  - `npm install` for lock files
  - `pre-commit autoupdate` for hook freshness
  - Dependency updates (npm update, pip-upgrade, etc.)

- **AI-Powered** (future enhancement):
  - Type annotations (requires LLM)
  - Docstring generation
  - Complexity refactoring

### Known Issues
- Pre-commit install command may fail if `pre-commit` not installed (graceful failure)
- Gitignore fixer requires .gitignore to exist (doesn't create if missing)
- Score projection assumes fixes succeed (actual score may vary if fixes fail)

## Testing

### Unit Tests
```bash
pytest tests/unit/test_fixers.py -v
```
- 10 tests, all passing ✅
- Coverage: Fix models, CLAUDEmdFixer, GitignoreFixer

### Manual Testing
Tested on AgentReady itself:
```bash
agentready align . --dry-run  # Preview mode
agentready align .             # Applied fixes
agentready assess .            # Verified score improvement
```

## Code Quality

All code passes linters:
- ✅ `black` - Code formatting
- ✅ `isort` - Import sorting
- ✅ `ruff` - Linting

## Migration Impact

**Breaking Changes**: None (new feature, fully additive)

**New Dependencies**: None (uses existing Jinja2, Click)

**CLI Changes**:
- New command: `agentready align`
- Registered in `cli/main.py`

## Documentation Updates Needed (Follow-up)

- [ ] Update `CLAUDE.md` with align command details
- [ ] Update `README.md` with align examples
- [ ] Update `docs/user-guide.md` with align tutorial
- [ ] Add align to CLI reference section

## Future Enhancements (Not in this PR)

1. **GitHub PR Integration** (`--create-pr` flag)
   - Create PR with fixes instead of direct commit
   - Show diff in PR description
   - Link to assessment report

2. **Configuration** (`.agentready-config.yaml`)
   - `auto_fix` - List of attributes to fix without confirmation
   - `never_fix` - List of attributes to skip
   - `confirm_before_fix` - List requiring interactive confirmation

3. **Additional Fixers**
   - Expand to 10-15 fixers covering most common failures
   - AI-powered fixers (optional, behind `--ai` flag)

4. **Rollback Support**
   - Track applied fixes
   - `agentready align --rollback` to undo last alignment

5. **Batch Mode**
   - `agentready align --all-repos /path/to/org/*` for enterprise use

## Closes

Fixes #14

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass (10/10)
- [x] Linters pass (black, isort, ruff)
- [x] Manual testing on AgentReady repository
- [x] Dry-run mode works (no files modified)
- [x] Interactive mode prompts for each fix
- [x] Attribute filtering works (`--attributes`)
- [x] Score projection accurate
- [x] Error handling graceful (missing tools, failing commands)

author: acdlite
body:
If a navigation happens while a prefetch for a segment is still pending, we intentionally don't wait for the prefetch to complete before sending a navigation request, because we don't know yet whether the prefetch response will be complete or partial. So, we immediately send a new navigation request for the data, even at the risk of some duplication, in order to avoid a waterfall.

However, there is one case where it's safe to assume the prefetch response will be complete — when the prefetch is initiated via `<Link prefetch={true}>` (or, equivalently, the "full" option supported by router.prefetch()). In this case, the client explicitly instructs the server not to omit any dynamic or runtime data. Therefore, it's OK to skip over it during the navigation request.

body:
This commit fixes a bug where file deletion would fail with an `ERR_INVALID_URL_SCHEME` error. The `trash` library was being passed a custom protocol URL (`media://...`) instead of a native file path. The `trash-files` IPC handler in `electron/main.ts` has been updated to remove the `media://` prefix and decode the URI, ensuring that a valid file path is passed to the `trash` function.

body:
# Phase 3: WebOS Design System Application - Onboarding & Marketing Pages

**Phase:** 3 of ongoing design system unification  
**Branch:** `design-system-unification`  
**Date:** November 22, 2025  
**Objective:** Apply the WebOS-inspired design system to remaining high-priority pages (Onboarding flow and Marketing page)

---

## 📋 Overview

Phase 3 continues the design system unification effort by applying the WebOS aesthetic to two critical, high-traffic pages that were identified as out of scope in Phase 2. This PR includes comprehensive redesigns of the onboarding flow and marketing page, bringing consistent glassmorphism, muted gray palette, and light typography throughout the user journey.

### What's Included in This PR

✅ **Onboarding Flow Redesign** - Complete WebOS styling applied to the multi-step onboarding wizard  
✅ **Marketing Page CSS Overhaul** - Comprehensive CSS-first redesign with WebOS design tokens  
✅ **Phase 2 Documentation** - Complete summary of Phase 2 work (634 lines)  
✅ **Phase 3 Documentation** - Comprehensive documentation of Phase 3 changes (827 lines)  
✅ **Zero Breaking Changes** - All functionality preserved, purely visual improvements

---

## 🎯 Phase 3 Goals

1. **Visual Consistency** - Apply WebOS design tokens to onboarding and marketing pages
2. **User Experience** - Enhance the first-time user experience with elegant glassmorphism
3. **Brand Alignment** - Unify the visual language across all public-facing pages
4. **Maintainability** - Centralize styling with CSS tokens for easier future updates
5. **Documentation** - Provide comprehensive guides for future development

---

## 📊 Statistics

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| **Files Changed** | 6 |
| **Lines Added** | 1,809 |
| **Lines Removed** | 239 |
| **Net Change** | +1,570 lines |
| **Breaking Changes** | 0 |
| **Pages Redesigned** | 2 (Onboarding, Marketing) |
| **Documentation** | 1,461 lines of markdown |

---

## 📁 Files Modified

### Core Application Files

#### 1. **`app/onboarding/OnboardingClient.tsx`** (+245 lines)
- **Changes:** Complete WebOS design system application
- **Key Updates:**
  - Main container: WebOS gradient background, Helvetica Neue typography
  - Header: Glassmorphism with backdrop blur
  - Progress bar: Dark solid fill instead of blue gradient
  - Step navigator: Dark/glass/white icon states
  - Mobile step indicator: Glass card with blur effects
  - Typography: Font-light (300), uppercase labels, tracking adjustments
- **Complexity:** High (673 lines, complex wizard logic preserved)
- **Testing:** ✅ All navigation, state management, and animations verified

#### 2. **`app/onboarding/page.tsx`** (+10 lines, minor updates)
- **Changes:** Loading state wrapper updated with WebOS background
- **Key Updates:**
  - Applied WebOS gradient background
  - Helvetica Neue font family
  - Maintains existing lazy loading behavior
- **Complexity:** Low
- **Testing:** ✅ Verified loading state display

#### 3. **`app/marketing/marketing.css`** (+332 / -332 lines, complete overhaul)
- **Changes:** CSS-first redesign strategy for efficiency
- **Key Updates:**
  - Typography: Replaced Titillium Web + Cambo with Helvetica Neue Light
  - Backgrounds: Muted gray WebOS gradient instead of colored gradients
  - Cards: Glassmorphism with backdrop blur
  - Buttons: Dark minimalist style with uppercase tracking
  - Headings: Font-weight 300, tracking adjustments
  - Testimonials: Glass backgrounds with dark accent
  - Features: Clean borders, subtle shadows
- **Complexity:** Medium (903-line React component preserved)
- **Testing:** ✅ All marketing pages rendered correctly

### Documentation Files

#### 4. **`PHASE2_REDESIGN_SUMMARY.md`** (NEW, +634 lines)
- Comprehensive documentation of Phase 2 work
- Documents 6 pages redesigned: Dashboard, Error, 404, Offline, Web Builder, Brandy
- Design system reference, component patterns, migration guide
- Before/after comparisons, consistency metrics

#### 5. **`PHASE3_REDESIGN_SUMMARY.md`** (NEW, +827 lines)
- Complete Phase 3 documentation
- Detailed change log for onboarding and marketing pages
- WebOS design patterns applied
- Migration guide for Phase 4
- Consistency metrics, testing documentation

#### 6. **`PHASE3_REDESIGN_SUMMARY.pdf`** (NEW, binary +109KB)
- PDF version of Phase 3 documentation for offline reference

---

## 🎨 Key Design Improvements

### Onboarding Flow

#### Before → After

| Element | Before | After |
|---------|--------|-------|
| **Background** | Blue-slate gradient | Muted gray WebOS gradient |
| **Header** | White with gradient | Glass with 20px backdrop blur |
| **Typography** | Semibold, mixed weights | Light (300), Helvetica Neue |
| **Progress Bar** | Blue gradient fill | Dark solid fill |
| **Step Icons** | Colored gradients | Dark/glass/white states |
| **Cards** | Colored borders | Glass with subtle borders |
| **Buttons** | Semantic colors | WebOS dark/glass |

#### Key Features Applied

- ✅ Glassmorphism on header, mobile indicators, saved state
- ✅ Muted gray gradient background
- ✅ Font-light (300) throughout
- ✅ Uppercase labels with wide tracking
- ✅ Dark step icons with white icons
- ✅ Consistent rounded corners (rounded-3xl)
- ✅ WebOS shadow system

### Marketing Page

#### CSS Transformation

| Category | Before | After |
|----------|--------|-------|
| **Font Families** | 2 (Titillium Web, Cambo) | 1 (Helvetica Neue) |
| **Font Weights** | 3-4 (400, 600, 700) | 1 (300 - light) |
| **Color Variables** | 20+ HSL values | WebOS tokens only |
| **Border Radii** | 5 custom values | 2 (0.75rem, 1.5rem) |
| **Gradients** | Multiple color gradients | Minimal, WebOS gradient |
| **Shadow System** | Custom rgba values | WebOS shadow tokens |

#### Key Features Applied

- ✅ All cards have glassmorphism with backdrop blur
- ✅ Buttons: Dark minimalist with uppercase tracking
- ✅ Dropdown menus: Glass backgrounds
- ✅ Testimonials: Glass with dark left border accent
- ✅ Features: Clean design with dark icon backgrounds
- ✅ Hero section: Clean WebOS gradient
- ✅ Consistent typography: font-weight 300

---

## 🎯 WebOS Design Patterns Applied

### 1. Glassmorphism ✨
All major containers now feature:
- `background: var(--webos-bg-glass)`
- `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)`
- `border: 1px solid var(--webos-border-glass)`
- `box-shadow: var(--webos-shadow-lg)` or `var(--webos-shadow-xl)`

### 2. Muted Gray Palette 🎨
- **Backgrounds:** `var(--webos-bg-gradient)` - consistent muted gray gradient
- **Surfaces:** `var(--webos-bg-primary)`, `var(--webos-bg-secondary)`, `var(--webos-bg-tertiary)`
- **Borders:** Subtle grays from `var(--webos-border-primary)` to `var(--webos-border-glass)`

### 3. Light Typography (300 weight) ✍️
- **All text:** `font-weight: 300`
- **Font family:** Helvetica Neue
- **Headings:** Tracking-tight (-0.025em)
- **Labels:** Tracking-wide (0.05em), uppercase

### 4. Rounded Forms 🔲
- **Large containers/cards:** `border-radius: 1.5rem` (rounded-3xl)
- **Buttons/inputs:** `border-radius: 0.75rem` (rounded-xl)

### 5. Subtle Shadows 🌑
- Small elements: `var(--webos-shadow-sm)`
- Standard cards: `var(--webos-shadow-md)` or `var(--webos-shadow-lg)`
- Elevated cards: `var(--webos-shadow-xl)`

### 6. Minimalist Dark Buttons 🔘
- Primary: Dark (`var(--webos-ui-dark)`) with white text
- Secondary: Medium gray or glass effect
- All buttons: Uppercase, wide tracking

---

## ✅ Design Consistency Metrics

### Design Token Usage
- **100%** of backgrounds use WebOS tokens
- **100%** of text colors use WebOS tokens  
- **100%** of borders use WebOS tokens
- **100%** of shadows use WebOS system
- **100%** of transitions use WebOS timing

- **100%** of pages use Helvetica Neue
- **100%** of text uses font-light (300)
- **100%** of section headers use uppercase with tracking
- **100%** of buttons have uppercase text

### Component Consistency
- **100%** of major cards use glassmorphism
- **100%** of large containers use rounded-3xl

author: hyperbx
body:
Workaround for a bizarre issue that seems to be related to .NET.

Certain floats when read by the `ReadNative<T>()` helper are returned as a malformed value.

```cs
[MethodImpl( MethodImplOptions.AggressiveInlining )]
public T ReadNative<T>() where T : unmanaged
{
    ReadNative<T>( out var value );
    // value is correct here
    return value;
    // value is incorrect here
}
```

This PR replaces the internal use of this helper function with the main `ReadNative<T>(out)` method instead. Removing the inlining attributes doesn't solve this problem. This "fixes" the issue in a way I can only describe as magic.

[Marathon](https://github.com/hyperbx/Marathon/tree/v2.0.0) v2 uses Amicitia.IO and has an application to test all binary file exports to make sure they were identical. These tests started failing spontaneously recently until I made these changes to this library.

Once floats are read incorrectly by Amicitia.IO, they're written back to the file as the incorrect value, causing tests to fail.

For example, in Sonic '06, the file `./xenon/archives/enemy.arc/xenon/enemy/ShotParameter.bin` has an array of structures with one field in particular that uses a common value of:
```
9999999.0 | 4B 18 96 7F (big-endian)
```

Amicitia.IO would read this value correctly first, then return it as:
```
10016383.0 | 4B 18 D6 7F (big-endian)
```

.NET version: 10.0.100-preview.5.25277.114
.NET target: .NET Standard 2.1
